passage:
The community center built a small outdoor stage in the park. Anyone could use it after registering.
At first, only musicians performed there. Later, children used it for puppet shows, students practiced speeches, and grandparents taught folk songs.
One evening, a girl read a poem she had written. Her voice shook, but people listened quietly. After she finished, an old man said, "Thank you for giving your words to the evening."
The girl smiled.
The stage was small, but it changed the park. People no longer only walked through it. They stopped, watched, and shared.
A public space becomes more alive when ordinary people are invited to add something of their own.
